[[File:Example of cyclic sieving with tableaux.svg|thumb|A ''q''-analogue of the [[hook length formula]] exhibits cyclic sieving, with evaluations at roots of unity counting the number of rectangular standard [[Young tableaux]] fixed by repeated applications of [[jeu de taquin]] promotion.]]

In [[combinatorics|combinatorial mathematics]], '''cyclic sieving''' is a phenomenon in which an integer [[polynomial]] evaluated at certain [[root of unity|roots of unity]] counts the rotational symmetries of a [[finite set]].<ref>{{cite journal|first1=Victor|last1=Reiner|first2=Dennis|last2=Stanton|first3=Dennis|last3=White|title=What is... Cyclic Sieving?|journal=[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]]|volume=61|issue=2|date=February 2014|pages=169–171|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/201402/rnoti-p169.pdf|doi=10.1090/noti1084|doi-access=free}}</ref>  Given a family of cyclic sieving phenomena, the polynomials give a [[Q-analog|''q''-analogue]] for the enumeration of the sets, and often arise from an underlying algebraic structure, such as a [[representation theory|representation]].

The first study of cyclic sieving was published by Reiner, Stanton and White in 2004.<ref>{{cite journal |first1=V. |last1=Reiner |first2=D. |last2=Stanton |first3=D. |last3=White |title=The cyclic sieving phenomenon |journal=Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series A |volume=108 |issue=1 |pages=17–50 |year=2004 |doi=10.1016/j.jcta.2004.04.009 |doi-access=free }}</ref> The phenomenon generalizes the "''q'' = −1 phenomenon" of [[John Stembridge]], which considers evaluations of the polynomial only at the first and second roots of unity (that is, ''q'' = 1 and ''q'' = −1).<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Stembridge |first1=John |title=Some hidden relations involving the ten symmetry classes of plane partitions |journal=Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series A |date=1994 |volume=68 |issue=2 |pages=372–409 |doi=10.1016/0097-3165(94)90112-0|hdl=2027.42/31216 |hdl-access=free }}</ref>

== Definition ==

For every positive integer <math>n</math>, let <math>\omega_n</math> denote the primitive <math>n</math><sup>th</sup> root of unity <math>e^{2\pi i/n}</math>.

Let <math>X</math> be a finite set with an [[group action|action]] of the cyclic group <math>C_n</math>, and let <math>f(q)</math> be an [[integer]] polynomial. The triple <math>(X,C_n,f(q))</math> exhibits the '''cyclic sieving phenomenon''' (or '''CSP''') if for every positive integer <math>d</math> dividing <math>n</math>, the number of elements in <math>X</math> fixed by the action of the subgroup <math>C_d</math> of <math>C_n</math> is equal to <math>f(\omega_d)</math>. If <math>C_n</math> acts as rotation by <math>2\pi/n</math>, this counts elements in <math>X</math> with <math>d</math>-fold [[rotational symmetry]].

Equivalently, suppose <math>\sigma:X\to X</math> is a [[bijection]] on <math>X</math> such that <math>\sigma^n=\rm{id}</math>, where <math>\rm{id}</math> is the identity map. Then <math>\sigma</math> induces an action of <math>C_n</math> on <math>X</math>, where a given [[Generating set of a group|generator]] <math>c</math> of <math>C_n</math> acts by <math>\sigma</math>. Then <math>(X,C_n,f(q))</math> exhibits the cyclic sieving phenomenon if the number of elements in <math>X</math> fixed by <math>\sigma^d</math> is equal to <math>f(\omega_n^d)</math> for every integer <math>d</math>.

==Example==

Let <math>X</math> be the 2-element subsets of <math>\{1, 2, 3, 4\}</math>. Define a bijection <math>\sigma:X\to X</math> which increases each element in the pair by one (and sends <math>4</math> back to <math>1</math>). This induces an action of <math>C_4</math> on <math>X</math>, which has an [[Group action#Orbits and stabilizers|orbit]]
<math display=block> \{1,3\}\mapsto\{2,4\}\mapsto\{1,3\}</math>
of size two and an orbit
<math display=block>\{1, 2\} \mapsto \{2, 3\} \mapsto \{3, 4\} \mapsto \{1, 4\} \mapsto \{1, 2\}</math>
of size four. If <math>f(q)=1+q+2q^2+q^3+q^4</math>, then <math>f(1)=6</math> is the number of elements in <math>X</math>, <math>f(i)=0</math> counts fixed points of <math>\sigma</math>, <math>f(-1)=2</math> is the number of fixed points of <math>\sigma^2</math>, and <math>f(-i)=0</math> is the number of fixed points of <math>\sigma^3</math>. Hence, the triple <math>(X,C_4,f(q))</math> exhibits the cyclic sieving phenomenon.

More generally, set <math>[n]_q:=1+q+\cdots+q^{n-1}</math> and define the [[Q-binomial coefficient|''q''-binomial coefficient]] by
<math display=block>\left[{n \atop k}\right]_q = \frac{[n]_q\cdots [2]_q[1]_q}{[k]_q\cdots [2]_q[1]_q[n-k]_q\cdots [2]_q[1]_q}.</math>
which is an integer polynomial evaluating to the usual [[binomial coefficient]] at <math>q=1</math>. For any positive integer <math>d</math> dividing <math>n</math>,
:<math>\left[{n \atop k}\right]_{\omega_d} = \begin{cases}\left({n/d \atop k/d}\right)&\text{if }d\mid k,\\
0 & \text{otherwise}.\end{cases}</math>

If <math>X_{n,k}</math> is the set of size-<math>k</math> subsets of <math>\{1,\dots,n\}</math> with <math>C_n</math> acting by increasing each element in the subset by one (and sending <math>n</math> back to <math>1</math>), and if <math>f_{n,k}(q)</math> is the ''q''-binomial coefficient above, then <math>(X_{n,k},C_n,f_{n,k}(q))</math> exhibits the cyclic sieving phenomenon for every <math>0\leq k\leq n</math>.<ref>{{cite journal |first1=V. |last1=Reiner |first2=D. |last2=Stanton |first3=D. |last3=White |title=The cyclic sieving phenomenon |journal=Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series A |volume=108 |issue=1 |pages=17–50 |year=2004 |doi=10.1016/j.jcta.2004.04.009 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

== In representation theory ==

The cyclic sieving phenomenon can be naturally stated in the language of representation theory. The group action of <math>C_n</math> on <math>X</math> is linearly extended to obtain a representation, and the decomposition of this representation into irreducibles determines the required coefficients of the polynomial <math>f(q)</math>.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Sagan |first1=Bruce |title=The cyclic sieving phenomenon: a survey |date=2011 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |pages=183–234 | isbn=978-1-139-50368-6}}</ref>

Let <math>V=\mathbb{C}(X)</math> be the [[vector space]] over the [[complex number]]s with a [[basis (mathematics)|basis]] indexed by a finite set <math>X</math>. If the cyclic group <math>C_n</math> acts on <math>X</math>, then linearly extending each action turns <math>V</math> into a representation of <math>C_n</math>.

For a generator <math>c</math> of <math>C_n</math>, its action on <math>\mathbb{C}(X)</math> is given by a [[permutation matrix]] <math>[c]</math>, and the [[Trace (linear algebra)|trace]] of <math>[c]^d</math> counts the elements of <math>X</math> fixed by <math>c^d</math>. In particular, the triple <math>(X,C_n,f(q))</math> exhibits the cyclic sieving phenomenon if and only if <math>f(\omega_n^d)=\chi(c^d)</math> for every <math>0\leq d<n</math>, where <math>\chi</math> is the [[Character (mathematics)#Character of a representation|character]] of <math>V</math>.

This gives a method for determining <math>f(q)</math>. For every integer <math>k</math>, let <math>V^{(k)}</math> be the one-dimensional representation of <math>C_n</math> in which <math>c</math> acts as [[scalar multiplication]] by <math>\omega_n^k</math>. For an integer polynomial <math display=inline>f(q)=\sum_{k\geq 0}m_kq^k</math>, the triple <math>(X,C_n,f(q))</math> exhibits the cyclic sieving phenomenon if and only if
<math display=block>V\cong\bigoplus_{k\geq 0}m_kV^{(k)}.</math>

==Further examples==

===Words===
Let <math>W</math> be a finite set of [[combinatorics on words|words]] of the form <math>w=w_1\cdots w_n</math> where each letter <math>w_j</math> is an integer and <math>W</math> is closed under permutation (that is, if <math>w</math> is in <math>W</math>, then so is any [[anagram]] of <math>w</math>). The ''major index'' of a word <math>w</math> is the sum of all indices <math>j</math> such that <math>w_j>w_{j+1}</math>, and is denoted <math>{\rm{maj}}(w)</math>.

If <math>C_n</math> acts on <math>W</math> by rotating the letters of each word, and
<math display=block>f(q)=\sum_{w\in W}q^{{\rm{maj}}(w)}</math>
then <math>(W,C_n,f(q))</math> exhibits the cyclic sieving phenomenon.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Berget |first1=Andrew |last2=Eu |first2=Sen-Peng |last3=Reiner |first3=Victor |title=Constructions for Cyclic Sieving Phenomena |journal=SIAM Journal on Discrete Mathematics |date=2011 |volume=25 |issue=3 |pages=1297–1314 |doi=10.1137/100803596|arxiv=1004.0747 }}</ref>

=== Rectangular standard Young tableaux ===

Let <math>\lambda</math> be a [[integer partition|partition]] of size <math>n</math> with rectangular shape, and let <math>X_\lambda</math> be the set of [[Young tableau|standard Young tableaux]] with shape <math>\lambda</math>. [[Jeu de taquin]] promotion gives an action of <math>C_n</math> on <math>X</math>. Let <math>f(q)</math> be the following ''q''-analog of the [[hook length formula]]:
<math display=block>f_\lambda(q)=\frac{[n]_q\cdots [1]_q}{\prod_{(i,j)\in \lambda} [h(i,j)]_q}.</math>
Then <math>(X_\lambda,C_n,f_\lambda(q))</math> exhibits the cyclic sieving phenomenon. If <math>\chi_\lambda</math> is the character for the [[Representation theory of the symmetric group|irreducible representation of the symmetric group]] associated to <math>\lambda</math>, then <math>f_\lambda(\omega_n^d)=\pm\chi_\lambda(c^d)</math> for every <math>0\leq d<n</math>, where <math>c</math> is the [[Permutation#cycle notation|long cycle]] <math>(12\cdots n)</math>.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Madonald |first1=Ian |title=Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials |date=1995 |publisher=Oxford University Press |location=Oxford |isbn=9780198534891}}</ref>

If <math>Y</math> is the set of semistandard Young tableaux of shape <math>\lambda</math> with entries in <math>\{1,\dots,k\}</math>, then promotion gives an action of the cyclic group <math>C_k</math> on <math>Y_\lambda</math>. Define <math display=inline>\kappa(\lambda)=\sum_i(i-1)\lambda_i</math> and
<math display=block>g(q)=q^{-\kappa(\lambda)}s_\lambda(1,q,\dots,q^{k-1}),</math>
where <math>s_\lambda</math> is the [[Schur polynomial]]. Then <math>(Y,C_k,g(q))</math> exhibits the cyclic sieving phenomenon.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Rhoades|first1=Brendon|title=Cyclic sieving, promotion, and representation theory|journal=Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series A|date=January 2010|volume=117|issue=1|pages=38–76|doi=10.1016/j.jcta.2009.03.017|arxiv=1005.2568|s2cid=6294586}}</ref>

=== Non-crossing configurations ===

If <math>X</math> is the set of non-crossing (1,2)-configurations of <math>\{1,\dots,n-1\}</math>, then <math>C_{n-1}</math> acts on these by rotation. Let <math>f(q)</math> be the following ''q''-analog of the <math>n</math><sup>th</sup> [[Catalan number]]:
<math display=block>f(q)=\frac{1}{[n+1]_q}\left[{2n \atop n}\right]_q.</math>
Then <math>(X,C_{n-1},f(q))</math> exhibits the cyclic sieving phenomenon.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Thiel|first1=Marko|title=A new cyclic sieving phenomenon for Catalan objects|journal=Discrete Mathematics|date=March 2017|volume=340|issue=3|pages=426–9|doi=10.1016/j.disc.2016.09.006|arxiv=1601.03999|s2cid=207137333}}</ref>

=== Square semi-standard Young tableaux ===

Let <math>X</math> be the set of semi-standard Young tableaux of shape <math>(n,n)</math> with maximal entry <math>2n-k</math>, where entries along each row and column are strictly increasing. If <math>C_{2n-k}</math> acts on <math>X</math> by <math>K</math>-promotion and
<math display=block>f(q)=q^{n+\binom{k}{2}} \frac{\left[{n-1 \atop k}\right]_q \left[{2n-k \atop n-k-1}\right]_q}{ [n-k]_q},</math>
then <math>(X,C_{2n-k},f(q))</math> exhibits the cyclic sieving phenomenon.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Pechenik|first1=Oliver|title=Cyclic sieving of increasing tableaux and small Schröder paths|journal=Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series A|date=July 2014|volume=125|pages=357–378|doi=10.1016/j.jcta.2014.04.002|arxiv=1209.1355|s2cid=18693328}}</ref>

=== Permutations of a fixed cycle type ===

Let <math>S_{\lambda,j}</math> be the set of [[permutations]] of cycle type <math>\lambda</math> with exactly <math>j</math> exceedances. Conjugation gives an action of <math>C_n</math> on <math>S_{\lambda,j}</math>, and if
<math display=block>a_{\lambda,j}(q)=\sum_{\sigma \in S_{\lambda,j} }q^{\operatorname{maj}(\sigma)-j}</math>
then <math>(S_{\lambda,j}, C_n, a_{\lambda,j}(q))</math> exhibits the cyclic sieving phenomenon.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Sagan|first1=Bruce|last2=Shareshian|first2=John|last3=Wachs|first3=Michelle L.|title=Eulerian quasisymmetric functions and cyclic sieving|journal=Advances in Applied Mathematics|date=January 2011|volume=46|issue=1–4|pages=536–562|doi=10.1016/j.aam.2010.01.013|arxiv=0909.3143|s2cid=379574}}</ref>
